record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: For hit-and-run or the ball walk on a convex body, is there a single deterministic starting point—such as the centroid—that yields the same asymptotic convergence rate as starting from a warm start? More specifically, if one of these walks is started at the centroid, does it mix as fast as when initialized from a random point drawn from a warm-start distribution?

evidence.quote: Open problems. One open problem for both hit-and-run and the ball walk is to find a single starting point that is as good a start as a warm start. E.g., does one of these walks started at the centroid converge at the same rate as starting from a random point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body (a compact convex set with nonempty interior). Consider the following two Markov chains on $K$:

(i) The ball walk with radius $\delta>0$: from a point $x \in K$, pick a uniformly random point $y$ in the Euclidean ball of radius $\delta$ centered at $x$; move to $y$ if $y \in K$, otherwise stay at $x$.

(ii) Hit-and-run: from a point $x \in K$, choose a uniformly random line $\ell$ through $x$, and move to a point chosen uniformly at random from the chord $\ell \cap K$.

Both walks are reversible with respect to the uniform distribution on $K$. A "warm start" is an initial distribution $\mu_0$ on $K$ whose density with respect to the uniform distribution on $K$ is bounded by a constant (e.g., at most $2$). It is known that from such a warm start, both walks mix to within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution in $O^*(n^2 R^2/r^2)$ steps (where $K$ contains a ball of radius $r$ and is contained in a ball of radius $R$, and $O^*$ hides polylogarithmic factors).

Question: Does there exist a single deterministic starting point $x_0 \in K$ — for instance the centroid of $K$ — from which the ball walk (respectively, hit-and-run) achieves the same asymptotic mixing time bound (up to polylogarithmic factors in $n$, $R/r$, and $1/\varepsilon$) as it does from a warm-start distribution?
artifact.category_tag: Mixing of random walks on convex bodies
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources indicate that this remains an open question: it is still unknown whether the ball walk or hit-and-run started from a single canonical interior point such as the centroid mixes as fast as from a warm start. Hit-and-run is known to mix from any interior point but with a worse dependence than from a warm start, while the ball walk can be exponentially slow from bad starting points.

status_evidence.title: Hit-and-Run from a Corner (Lovász–Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Hit-and-run mixes from any interior point, but bounds depend on distance to boundary; warm start gives the best known bound.
status_evidence.claim: Mixing-time bounds for hit-and-run from a deterministic point are weaker than from a warm start.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Convex Geometry survey (Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem: find a single starting point that is as good as a warm start; e.g., does the walk started at the centroid converge at the same rate?
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether starting at the centroid yields the same mixing rate as a warm start is listed as open.
